title: State Power vs Human Dignity: The Debate Over Public Shaming of Accused
description: Context: A vacation bench of the Calcutta High Court sharply criticized the West Bengal state police for publicly parading accused individuals with ropes tied around their waists and circulating the videos on social media. About State Power vs Human Dignity: The Debate Over Public Shaming of Accused Legal and Statutory Framework Governing Restraints: Key Judicial Precedents and Constitutional Principles: Ethical Theories Associated with Penal Administration Challenges to Preserving Institutional Integrity: The public parading of accused individuals reveals a troubling gap between state power and the constitutional promise of human dignity. As the Calcutta High Court observed, the authority to arrest does not grant a license to publicly defame or humiliate a citizen before they have faced a fair trial. Is the campaign of naming and shaming of sexual offenders an ethical and appropriate way to bring justice to victims? Discuss the ethical issues involved in such campaigns. (150 Words)
